ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Recurrent pneumonia in one location

A 4-year-old has had three episodes of right lower-lobe pneumonia over four months. Between episodes, a focal wheeze persists. The family recalls a severe coughing spell while he played with small toy parts before the first illness. What underlying problem should be prioritized?

  1. Retained bronchial foreign body
  2. Cystic fibrosis
  3. Primary immunodeficiency
  4. Recurrent viral-triggered asthma
  5. Primary ciliary dyskinesia
Answer and explanation

Retained bronchial foreign body

A retained object can cause chronic focal obstruction and repeated infection in the same region.

Option explanations

Retained bronchial foreign body: A retained object can cause chronic focal obstruction and repeated infection in the same region.

Cystic fibrosis: This can cause repeated chest infections, but the abrupt onset and persistent single-lobe pattern favor local obstruction.

Primary immunodeficiency: This generally raises concern for infections at multiple sites or a broader pattern rather than the very focal postchoking course.

Recurrent viral-triggered asthma: Asthma is less likely to produce repeated bacterial consolidation in one lobe after a single choking event.

Primary ciliary dyskinesia: Longstanding airway symptoms and other characteristic features would be expected; the aspiration history is more compelling.
